cards.headline: EU businesses get more time and clearer routes for meeting some AI rules
cards.narrative: The EU's AI Omnibus entered into force on 27 July. It extends some compliance timelines, broadens support for smaller and mid-sized companies, and creates more room for supervised testing. Businesses still need to identify which AI Act duties already apply and which have moved.
applies_to: Small and mid-sized companies using AI in the EU
Companies developing AI systems for the EU market
cards.reason: The law is active, but the practical effect depends on company size, AI use and risk category.
cards.trigger: The EU AI Act Service Desk or a national regulator confirms the rules and dates that apply to your use case.
cards.verification_warning: This is regulatory information, not legal advice.

evidence.claim: The AI Omnibus entered into force on 27 July 2026.
evidence.source_text: On 27 July 2026, the AI Omnibus enters into force across the EU.

evidence.claim: The changes extend timelines and support smaller companies.
evidence.source_text: It supports innovation and competitiveness by easing compliance for smaller businesses.

reasons: The European Commission confirms the measure and its business-facing changes.

cards.headline: Europe lets platforms resume scanning some private messages for abuse material
cards.narrative: The EU has reinstated temporary rules allowing online services to voluntarily detect and remove child sexual abuse material until April 2028. Parliament narrowed the measure and excluded end-to-end encrypted communications. Negotiations on a permanent system are still continuing.
applies_to: People and companies using messaging services in the EU
Online communication platforms operating in the EU
cards.reason: The temporary rule is back, but platform implementation and the permanent law remain unsettled.
cards.trigger: A messaging provider changes its privacy terms or the EU agrees the permanent detection framework.
cards.verification_warning: The final permanent framework is still under negotiation.

evidence.claim: The temporary detection measure was reinstated until 3 April 2028.
evidence.source_text: The measure will be reinstated until 3 April 2028.

evidence.claim: End-to-end encrypted communications were excluded by Parliament.
evidence.source_text: exclude communications to which end-to-end encryption is, has been or will be applied

reasons: Council and Parliament records support the status, duration and encryption limitation.

cards.headline: EU businesses must start labelling some AI conversations and content on 2 August
cards.narrative: New EU transparency duties start on 2 August 2026. Some AI systems must tell people when they are interacting with AI, and some generated or altered content must be machine-readable. Businesses may also need to disclose deepfakes and AI-generated public-interest content.
applies_to: Businesses offering AI interactions in the EU
Teams publishing AI-generated content for EU audiences
cards.reason: The start date is confirmed, but the exact duty depends on the system, content and role of the business.
cards.trigger: Your AI vendor, legal adviser or regulator confirms that one of your customer interactions or content types falls under Article 50.
cards.verification_warning: Businesses should obtain case-specific legal advice before treating this as a compliance instruction.

evidence.claim: Article 50 transparency obligations start on 2 August 2026.
evidence.source_text: transparency obligations, which start to apply on 2 August 2026

evidence.claim: The rules cover AI interactions and some generated or altered content.
evidence.source_text: inform users when they are directly interacting with an AI

reasons: The Commission guidance confirms the date and covered transparency duties.

cards.headline: Meta will alert parents when a teen tells its AI they may harm themselves
cards.narrative: Meta says supervising parents will receive an alert when a teen's Meta AI chat suggests suicide or self-harm risk. A person will review flagged chats before the alert is sent. Meta is also extending a stricter conversation setting to its AI experiences for teens.
applies_to: Parents using Instagram supervision tools
Organizations offering AI chat experiences to teenagers
cards.reason: The change raises important questions about safety intervention, privacy and human review in youth-facing AI.
cards.trigger: Meta publishes rollout regions and error data, or regulators issue rules for parental alerts from AI conversations.
cards.verification_warning: Meta has announced the safeguard but has not published performance data in this source.

evidence.claim: Supervising parents can be alerted to self-harm signals in teen chats.
evidence.source_text: proactively alert supervising parents if their teen's Meta AI chat suggests they may be at risk

evidence.claim: Flagged chats receive manual review before an alert.
evidence.source_text: all chats flagged by our AI will be manually reviewed before an alert is sent

reasons: Meta's announcement directly supports the alert and review process.

cards.headline: The privacy-focused Android alternative GrapheneOS is preparing for Android 17
cards.narrative: GrapheneOS says it has ported its privacy-focused phone system to Android 17 and that official releases are coming soon. Its July releases also continue security and browser updates. The practical question is when stable device support and app compatibility are confirmed.
applies_to: People considering a privacy-focused Android phone
Organizations evaluating higher-security mobile devices
cards.reason: The port exists, but an official stable release and confirmed device compatibility are the meaningful decision points.
cards.trigger: GrapheneOS publishes the stable Android 17 release and its supported-device and compatibility notes.
cards.verification_warning: The official Android 17 release was announced as upcoming, not generally available.

evidence.claim: GrapheneOS has been ported to Android 17.
evidence.source_text: GrapheneOS has been ported to Android 17

evidence.claim: Official releases are not yet available.
evidence.source_text: official releases are coming soon

reasons: The project's official announcements support both the port and upcoming-release status.

cards.headline: Travellers to the US may be asked to unlock phones and other devices at the border
cards.narrative: US Customs and Border Protection says officers may search phones, computers and cameras during border inspection, although it describes searches as rare. A civil-rights group reported growing demands involving journalists and travellers in July. The legal position and consequences can vary by citizenship and circumstance.
applies_to: International business travellers entering the United States
Organizations whose staff travel with sensitive company data
cards.reason: The authority already exists, while recent reports make device and company-data exposure a live travel risk.
cards.trigger: CBP changes its device-search directive, a court changes the legal standard, or an employer issues a formal travel-device policy.
cards.verification_warning: This card is not legal advice and does not prescribe how a traveller should respond to an officer.

evidence.claim: CBP officers may search electronic devices at ports of entry.
evidence.source_text: CBP officers may search a traveler's mobile phone, computer, camera, or other electronic devices

evidence.claim: CBP describes these searches as uncommon.
evidence.source_text: less than 0.01 percent of arriving international travelers

reasons: CBP confirms the authority and published frequency; July reporting provides the current signal.

cards.headline: Dubai now has a continuously updated digital copy of its buildings and infrastructure
cards.narrative: Dubai has launched a digital twin platform that mirrors buildings, facilities, infrastructure and master plans. The virtual copy is intended to stay updated as the city changes. This could affect how future property, planning and infrastructure decisions are tested before work begins.
applies_to: Dubai property and infrastructure businesses
Urban planners and real-estate technology teams
cards.reason: The platform is live, but business access, data-sharing rules and practical use cases are not yet clear.
cards.trigger: Dubai publishes access rules, partner programmes or commercial use cases for the Digital Twin Platform.
cards.verification_warning: The announcement does not define commercial access or pricing.

evidence.claim: Dubai launched a city-scale Digital Twin Platform.
evidence.source_text: Hamdan bin Mohammed witnesses launch of Dubai Digital Twin Platform

evidence.claim: The platform covers buildings and infrastructure with continuous updates.
evidence.source_text: incorporating comprehensive data covering facilities, landmarks, infrastructure, master plans, buildings

reasons: The official Dubai announcement confirms the launch and the platform's scope.

cards.headline: More US visa applicants must make their social media profiles public for screening
cards.narrative: The US State Department expanded screening for several visa categories, including H-1B, student and exchange visas. Applicants are instructed to set all social media profiles to public or open. The measure makes online history part of a wider immigration and workforce-planning issue.
applies_to: Employers sponsoring US visa applicants
Students and professionals applying for listed US visas
cards.reason: The instruction is active, but its operational and privacy impact varies by visa category and applicant.
cards.trigger: The State Department changes the covered visa list or publishes more detailed screening guidance.
cards.verification_warning: Applicants should rely on official visa instructions and qualified immigration advice.

evidence.claim: The expanded screening covers several work, student and family visa categories.
evidence.source_text: H-1B, H-4, F, M, and J nonimmigrant visas

evidence.claim: Applicants are instructed to make social profiles public.
evidence.source_text: adjust the privacy settings on all of their social media profiles to public or open

reasons: The State Department announcement directly supports the affected categories and instruction.

cards.headline: The US may ask visa-free visitors for five years of social media and phone history
cards.narrative: US Customs and Border Protection proposed making five years of social media history mandatory in ESTA applications. The proposal also lists past phone numbers, longer email history and family information. It was published as a proposed information collection, so travellers should not treat every field as final yet.
applies_to: Visa Waiver Program travellers to the United States
Businesses sending staff to the US under ESTA
cards.reason: The proposal could materially change travel preparation, but the final form and implementation date need confirmation.
cards.trigger: CBP publishes the final ESTA form, an effective date and the confirmed mandatory data fields.
cards.verification_warning: This is a proposal, not confirmation that every listed field is currently mandatory.

evidence.claim: The proposal would make five years of social media history mandatory for ESTA.
evidence.source_text: require ESTA applicants to provide their social media from the last 5 years

evidence.claim: The listed data fields include past telephone numbers.
evidence.source_text: Telephone numbers used in the last five years

reasons: The Federal Register notice supports the proposed fields; the card clearly labels them as proposed.

cards.headline: Manufacturers can now test decisions in virtual factories before changing the real one
cards.narrative: Dassault Systèmes launched virtual AI companions and Virtual Twin Factories for industrial work. The system combines a digital copy of operations with assistants for programme management, engineering and science. The promise is safer testing before changes reach physical production.
applies_to: Manufacturing and operations leaders
Engineering teams evaluating digital twins
cards.reason: The capability is available, but independent results, implementation effort and commercial terms are not established here.
cards.trigger: Dassault publishes pricing, deployment requirements and measured customer results for Virtual Twin Factories.
cards.verification_warning: This is a vendor announcement and does not independently prove operational savings.

evidence.claim: Dassault launched Virtual Twin Factories for industry.
evidence.source_text: Virtual Twin Factories for industries

evidence.claim: The new companions cover programme management, engineering and science.
evidence.source_text: AURA for program management, LEO for complex engineering and MARIE for deep science

reasons: The vendor announcement supports availability and scope; the card preserves uncertainty about outcomes.
